Partnered with Northwestern Fraternity & Sorority Life (FSL) and the Center for Student Advocacy and Wellness(CSAW)

name: Survivor: Northwestern
description: Survivor: Northwestern serves those interested in production and entertainment, creating a diverse and inclusive community for lovers of reality television and creators of narrative content, in pre- and post-production.

name: Tabletop Club
description: Help Northwestern students find and participate in roleplaying games, help them grow as roleplaying hobbyists, and provide an inclusive environment in which new players can engage with tabletop roleplaying.

name: Taiwanese American Students Association
description: TASA strives to spread awareness and appreciation of Taiwanese culture through campus and community outreach, as well as through philanthropic efforts.

name: TAMID Group
description: TAMID Group is a nonprofit organization that develops the professional skills of undergraduate students through hands-on interaction with Israeli businesses. TAMID at Northwestern is divided into two subgroups: consulting and investment fund. In both groups, students engage in experiential business opportunities with a focus on international economics. The mission of this club is to provide a positive learning experience for students interested in business and/or Israel, creating a sense of community both on campus and within TAMID’s national organization.

name: TBD
description: TBD strives to create accessible performance art that can be enjoyed even by those who do not like theatre. Through a non-fiction stage, the company members perform plays as themselves about real things they have experienced. Nothing is fabricated; rather, the performers choose personal and artistic ways to express their own truths. Because of the focus on the audience and the words of the playwrights/performers, TBD provides a uniquely accessible opportunity for students to have fun, laugh, and reflect on their own experiences.

name: Team Awareness Combating Overdose
description: Our mission is to combat drug overdose among young adults using research-based education and accessible harm-reduction supplies like fentanyl test strips.

name: TEDxNorthwesternU
description: TEDxNorthwesternU's mission is to spread "ideas worth sharing" in the Northwestern, Evanston, Chicago, and Global communities. This mission includes a yearly conference with 6-12 speakers held on Northwestern's campus in the spring. TEDxNorthwesternU is an independently organized TEDx conference.

name: TGS Cross-Cultural
description: We recognize that “…diversity is hollow unless…individuals…can communicate with each other” (MIT, diversity committee). The purpose of the graduate student diversity committee is to help promote and strengthen intercultural communication among graduate students. Furthermore, our organization aims to foster cultural competence among all graduate student groups. Cultural competence is an essential skill to any graduate student who enters our global workplace or academia. Accordingly, Northwestern graduate students will need an awareness of how to interact with people from other cultures—both kno

name: Thai Student Association
description: The Thai Student Association aims to foster a welcoming community for Thai students and those interested in Thai Culture at Northwestern University. The The organization strives to celebrate and share Thai culture through social and educational programming to support student connection and cross-cultural understanding.

name: The Bike Project
description: The purpose of The Bike Project is to promote cycling and casual bike riding as an accessible, sustainable, and social activity among students, having workshops teaching repair and maintenance, and organizing social group rides around Evanston. The Bike Project seeks to enhance the overall student experience by promoting the benefits of cycling while supporting inclusivity, sustainability, and personal empowerment and promoting a cheaper alternative to travel around campus and beyond.

name: The Bix
description: Our purpose on NU’s campus is to practice and perform musical improv within the context of the university. We are a performance group on campus that spends its time rehearsing and training to do fully improvised musicals.

name: The Blackout
description: The Blackout seeks to create a quality late-night show while providing a hands-on, fun, and community-based learning experience for all of its members.

name: The Campus Kitchen at Northwestern University
description: The mission of The Campus Kitchens Project is to use service as a tool to:* Strengthen Bodies by using existing resources to meet hunger and nutritional needs in our community;* Empower Minds by providing leadership and service learning opportunities to students, and educational benefits to adults, seniors, children, and families in need; and* Build Communities by fostering a new generation of community-minded adults through resourceful and mutually beneficial partnerships among students, social service agencies, businesses and schools.

name: The Club Ski Team
description: It is the mission of the Club Ski Team at Northwestern to foster an inclusive environment for those who love skiing and snow sports.

name: The Daily Northwestern
description: Northwestern and Evanston's only daily news source since 1881.

name: The Deep End
description: Inform and entertain members of the Northwestern community through comedic deep dives into local news.

name: The Dolphin Show
description: The Dolphin Show is a non-profit student theatre organization that annually produces the nation's largest student-run musical. It celebrates the diverse talents of the Northwestern University undergraduate community by providing opportunities to learn and excel in all artistic and administrative fields. The Dolphin Show presents a professional-caliber production, while involving the community through outreach.

name: The Film Festival
description: The Film Festival's purpose is to unify Northwestern undergraduate filmmaking within the Northwestern community, to raise awareness about Northwestern undergraduate films among Evanston, Chicago, and beyond, and to facilitate the transfer and appreciation of cinema between Northwestern and the rest of the artistic world. name: The Flipside
description: We here at The Northwestern Flipside strive to provide the Northwestern community with the finest and wittiest satire. Whether it be online, in print, or in video form, our goal is to satirize some of the biggest topics on campus and the world at large. We aim to provide members with a creative writing outlet that focuses on argumentative satire, similar to The Onion.

name: The Impact Movement at Northwestern University
description: The Impact Movement is a campus ministry organization engaging the church, the campus, and the community. Through our work, college students become disciples of Jesus Christ who successfully graduate from higher education with a consciousness towards improving the lives of those who are marginalized and on the fringes.

name: The Leukemia and Lymphoma Society Club at Northwestern
description: The Leukemia and Lymphoma Society (LLS) is a national organization at the forefront of the fight against blood cancers, supporting patients by funding research efforts, advocating for legislation which benefits patients, and providing financial assistance to current blood cancer patients. The LLS Club of Northwestern aims to support the national organization’s goals primarily through fundraising. We plan to participate in LLS’ Visionaries of the Year fundraising campaign in 2025. Additionally, we plan to host monthly panel discussions with healthcare professionals to spread awareness about blo

name: The MSGH SLC
description: The Northwestern University MSGH Student Leadership Council (SLC) is dedicated to supporting and connecting with prospective students, current students, and alumni in the Master of Science in Global Health program. The SLC aims to inspire and support the next generation of global health leaders by promoting knowledge and raising awareness of both the global health field and the MSGH graduate program at Northwestern University.

name: The Open Democracy
description: To make Participatory Budgeting a recurring process in Evanston by training and supporting student organizers.

name: The Panini Players
description: The Panini Players will provide the Northwestern, Evanston, and Chicagoland communities with exposure to the Commedia dell'Arte theatrical form for the education and entertainment of our audiences. We will introduce students to Commedia dell'Arte through our live feature performances and our public relations efforts.

name: The Set Up
description: Our mission is to provide a place for students to have a comfortable and fun place to try stand-up comedy. There is no dedicated organization for standup on campus, so it is important to provide a space dedicated solely to it. It will be a place where students can workshop and perform material, and it will be open to any who want to join.

name: The Undead Poets Society
description: The Undead Poets Society est. 2025 "Women Writing Weird Words" We are The Undead Poets Society, Northwestern's first women-and-femme-focused writing workshop! Our mission is to create a community of passionate creative writers who uplift each other socially, creatively, and professionally. We are not publication focused. Rather, our mission is to improve our craft together and have some fun along the way. Join for workshops, bonding events, and professional seminars all related to creative writing!

name: The Undertones
description: The Undertones aim to create a cappella music that can be shared and enjoyed on Northwestern’s campus, as well as with a national and international audience. More specifically, we hope: - To arrange original compositions of music, tailored to the genres of interest encompassed by the group’s current composition of members; - To put on quarterly concerts to share our original music with Northwestern University students, alumni, and the larger Evanston community; - To compete in the International Championship of Collegiate A Cappella; - To go on a week-long domestic or international tour, throug

name: The Waa-Mu Show
description: The Waa-Mu Show is Northwestern University’s own original musical, written, performed, and presented by Northwestern students.As Northwestern’s oldest theatrical tradition, The Waa-Mu Show provides undergraduates with the unparalleled opportunity to create an original musical each year. Students serve as leaders in every aspect of development from conception through production to create a show exploring themes and stories that inspire us as college students, challenge us as musical theatre artists, and engage us with our surrounding communities.The Waa-Mu Show strives to place itself at the fo

name: The Women's Network
description: Our mission at TWN is to create a community of women that celebrates the desire to achieve, cultivating their ambition and confidence and preparing them to be the next generation of innovators and leaders. TWN is a diverse and inclusive community that emphasizes the importance of building your network, celebrating ambition and connecting college students to each other and to leaders in a variety of fields. The Women’s Network is a national organization that exists on over 42 college campuses and counting.

name: The Youth Movement Against Alzheimer's
description: To promote understanding of Alzheimer's among youth by providing opportunities to help those affected by the disease.

name: Theme Park Engineering & Design
description: Our mission is to introduce students to the themed entertainment & roller coaster industry through hands-on engineering projects and competitions, providing a platform for theme park enthusiasts and creative engineers to collaborate and design whatever they can imagine, as well as supporting the professional development of students interested in careers within the themed entertainment industry.

name: THUNK A Cappella
description: THUNK a cappella is Northwestern University's oldest co-ed a cappella group. Since their beginning on campus in 1993, THUNK performs three shows every year on campus, while also performing at numerous external gigs on campus and in the Chicago area.

name: Tikkun Olam Makers
description: To serve our local community through engineering products that meet the unmet challenges of people with disabilities.

name: TONIK Tap
description: TONIK Tap is committed to expanding our presence on campus and in the greater Chicagoland area, ensuring success and accomplishment within the company, and promoting and generating greater awareness of and appreciation for the classic American art form of tap dance through strong technique, dynamic choreography, and quirky humor. Ultimately, we're shooting for a close-knit, creative community of tap dancers: one big, tappy family.

name: Track Club
description: Our mission is to have fun and run fast! We meet outside of SPAC every weekday at 5:30 for practice and compete at 4 meets per quarter on the weekends

name: Trading Card Game Club
description: Our goal is to help Northwestern students find groups to play trading card games, help them develop as trading card game players, and to provide an inclusive environment in which new and seasoned players alike can play trading card games together.

name: Transfer Student Organization
description: The purpose of the Transfer Student Organization is to support and strengthen the transfer community through social events, peer-mentorship, and information sharing.

name: Treblemakers
description: Treblemakers is Northwestern’s premier East Asian-interest a cappella group. Since our founding in 2004, we have strived to promote and celebrate Asian and Asian-American musical excellence both within and beyond the Northwestern community. We perform songs in a variety of different languages, such as English, Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Cantonese, Tagalog, and many more!

name: Tufaan Entertainment
description: Tufaan Entertainment is Northwestern's premier Bollywood-fusion dance competition aiming to raise awareness of South Asian culture in the US and promote education through the arts abroad.

name: Turkish Student Association
description: TSA is a student group aiming to bring the Turkish Students in Northwestern together, increase public awareness about Turkey in NU, and add to the diversity on campus. The Turkish Student Association (TSA) aims to gather Turkish students under one umbrella and create a supportive environment while introducing Turkish culture to Northwestern, thus creating a more diverse environment. Some of the events that TSA organizes are (but are not limited to): watching Turkish national team games (i.e., football [soccer], basketball), dinner organizations, national holiday celebrations, and many more. Al

name: Typhoon Dance Troupe
description: Typhoon Dance Troupe is a student organized dance group that highlights popular, classical, ethnic, and contemporary dances of East and Southeast Asia. Through the art of dance, we dedicate ourselves to displaying pieces of the regions' rich, diverse cultures and to promote more interest and appreciation in the community for those cultures.

name: Ukrainian Club
description: Ukrainian Club plans to host events open to the broader Northwestern community that highlight Ukrainian art, music, dance, and food and to bring awareness to injustices inflicted on Ukrainians during Russia's invasion through traditional and social media.

name: Undergraduate Chemistry Council
description: The Undergraduate Chemistry Council is Northwestern University's only student group for undergraduates interested in chemistry. Throughout the year, the UCC sponsors faculty talks, social events, and mentoring programs. We are always looking for new members to expand our group and help out with events. We are also dedicated to being a resource for all students who are majoring in, or just have an interest in, chemistry.

name: Undergraduate Economics Society
description: The Undergraduate Economics Society at Northwestern University was formed in 2005 to increase resources for students interested in economics and business and further their academic and career goals. The organization exists to provide a variety of events to enrich students’ experiences at Northwestern and to continue the pursuit for excellence in the events we host and sponsor.

name: Undergraduate International Student Advancement Council
description: The International Student Advancement Council's mission is to empower international students at Northwestern University by integrating resources, fostering cultural interconnection, and addressing unique academic and administrative challenges. We are committed to building a supportive and inclusive community that celebrates diversity, advocates for equitable policies, and enhances the overall experience of international students on our campus.

name: Undergraduate Latin American Law Association
description: The Undergraduate Latin American Law Association is an organization committed to fostering a community for Latino-identifying students interested in the legal field by providing a supportive platform for personal and professional growth while creating a space for cultural engagement. We aim to equip our members with the tools necessary to succeed as they navigate undergrad, law school prep and applications, and the legal field through events, workshops, resources, and meetings. We recognize the underrepresentation of Latinos in the legal profession, and seek to create a place at Northwestern w

name: Undergraduate Premedical Society
description: The purpose of Undergraduate Premedical Society is to provide undergraduate premedical and pre-health students at Northwestern University with a resource on campus that will help them pursue their life as premedical students. We strive to help guide students as they apply to medical school, as well as create a sense of community among other students interested in careers in the health field. Further, we strive to empower students in the medical school admissions process, as well as in their studies in required classes at Northwestern.

name: Undergraduate Prison Education Partnership
description: To use our resources as Northwestern students to support prison education initiatives while bringing awareness about education in the criminal legal system to the broader Northwestern community.

name: Undergraduate Psychology Association
description: UPA is dedicated to promoting community amongst all those interested in psychology! As the only barrier-free psychology club on campus, we welcome students of all majors to participate in academic and social events throughout the school year. Our primary goal is to help students learn more about psychology in a non-classroom setting, foster student-faculty connections, and facilitate the awareness of professional opportunities. Whether you’re a newly declared psych major looking to get involved in a lab, or an upperclassman seeking advice on how to refine your grad school application, UPA is h

name: Undergraduate Radio/Television/Film Student Association
description: URSA is made up of student representatives in the Radio/TV/Film department. We act as the liaison between the student body and the faculty. Our role is to relay students' questions, issues, concerns, complaints, and ideas about the curriculum to the faculty so that these problems can be solved. Our co-chairs attend monthly faculty meetings and meet with the department chairs regularly in order to ensure that the students are being heard and valued.

name: Undergraduate Real Estate Club
description: Our mission is to help prepare undergraduates at Northwestern enter the professional commericial real estate scene, through means such as networking, speaker events, and most importantly, technical real estate education.

name: UNICEF NU
description: The purpose of UNICEF NU is to bring the ideals and purposes of UNICEF to the Northwestern community. Our mission is threefold: to promote current UNICEF programs, to spread awareness about various children’s rights issues, and to help fundraise on behalf of UNICEF. UNICEF NU will seek to engage Northwestern University students in global health issues and encourage them to advocate for children’s rights. UNICEF NU will benefit the Northwestern community by connecting students to a major intergovernmental organization. Not only will UNICEF NU be the first Northwestern student group collaboratin

name: United Students for Veterans' Health
description: Our aim is to give back to the men and women who've given so much to us. Often veterans being treated at VA hospitals suffer from isolation which are compounded by debilitating mental diseases. As volunteers, we aim to engage with veterans in order to make them feel valued. Our goal is to create lasting relationships with veterans and students!

name: UNITY Charity Fashion Show
description: The purpose of the UNITY Charity Fashion Show is to celebrate fashion, philanthropy and diversity at Northwestern University. We hold fundraisers to raise money for a different charity each year, and emphasize diversity by picking models straight from our student body, regardless of shape, size, or color, as well as committee members from other Northwestern organizations. Our objective is to unite students and individuals in the community who are passionate about fashion, but also deliver a message about a charitable cause through this means. We hope to work with other organizations on campus

name: University Bible Fellowship
description: Our mission as an organization is outreach to students and providing a Christian community for students. We do so by having meetings regularly, organizing one-to-one bible studies, and spending time together outside of campus as well.

name: University Blood Initiative
description: Our mission is to create a sustainable and equitable blood supply for the good of all. Our vision is to continuously engage a national network of young, diverse blood donor advocates to ensure the issue of blood donation is never forgotten. Founded at the University of Chicago in 2017, the University Blood Initiative officially received 501(c)(3) nonprofit status in 2021, and has since expanded to chapters at dozens of universities across the country–and we’re still growing. Our chapters partner with local blood centers to promote community engagement, education, and blood donation.

name: University Christian Ministry
description: "Open Hearts, Open Minds" is our motto. Curious learners. Mindful believers. Community builders. Justice seekers.

name: Vertigo Productions
description: As Northwestern University’s only theatre organization exclusively dedicated to producing new student written work, Vertigo Productions seeks to:1. Support undergraduate student playwrights by providing resources and a platform for new play development and production2. Produce a season of full-fledged productions, staged readings, and workshops that utilize the artistic medium of the new play to uplift the voices of students and foster campus wide conversations about the issues and themes about which students are passionate3. name: Vibrant Colors Collective
description: Coming to you in living color is Vibrant Colors Collective (VC2), a Northwestern arts organization that strives to produce work centering BIPOC bodies and voices! We are devoted entirely to the platforming and development of BIPOC creativity and the training of new BIPOC artists. We aim to provide our collaborators, along with marginalized members of the Northwestern and greater Evanston community, the space to experience joy and celebrate their cultures both on and off the stage ❤️🧡💛💚💙💜

name: Vietnamese Student Association
description: The Vietnamese Student Association is an organization for all those who have an interest in the Vietnamese culture. The Vietnamese Student Association will provide Vietnamese American students with a forum to share their traditions and unique cultural perspectives with each other and all other organization members. We will foster inclusion of diversity by hosting a variety of social and cultural events, and we will establish a coherent and influential identity on campus and throughout the greater community. name: Water Polo
description: To advance the game of Water Polo and provide an inviting and engaging space to practice and play said game.

name: WAVE Productions
description: WAVE Productions (WAVE) is a self-supporting, not-for-profit student theatre company operating primarily on Northwestern University’s Evanston Campus. WAVE Productions exists to open the door to a better future. We strive to produce stories the campus needs by empowering our peer collaborators in pursuit of their passions and growth.To fulfill its responsibility to the Northwestern University campus and surrounding communities, WAVE sets for itself the following objectives:- To sustain and nourish a dynamic and progressive presence on campus in large part by fostering a diverse theatrical seas

name: We're In Physics
description: WIP (We're In Physics) is an undergraduate organization, an off-shoot of the Women in Physics group. WIP was formed to aid in the retention and enrich the experience of women and nonbinary undergraduate physics majors by providing profession development support, mentorship and community building. WIP is intentionally inclusive of those of underrepresented genders.

name: Wild Roots
description: Our mission is to connect students to the earth and each other, to serve the evolving educational and social needs of the Northwestern community, and to inspire students to think critically about the food we eat by starting conversations about sustainability, social justice, and our food system. We live our mission by growing fresh produce for the Northwestern and Evanston communities using sustainable practices and by using the garden as an educational tool to empower students to produce their own food, to creatively solve ecological problems, and to share their knowledge with others. Wild Ro

name: Wildcat Animate
description: Our mission is to learn about and apply concepts in animation in a dynamic, collaborative setting that is both accessible for newcomers and engaging for advanced artists. Our goal is to make students more comfortable with animation as medium for storytelling.

name: Wildcats for Israel
description: To raise awareness of Israel on campus and to educate students about Israeli affairs including culture, politics, and history in order to promote support for the state of Israel.

name: WildHacks
description: WildHacks is Northwestern University’s largest Hackathon, where students get together to build inspiring software projects.

name: WNUR News
description: WNUR News exists to provide high quality audio news programming to the Northwestern and Evanston communities on a regular basis. Through this programming, WNUR News will provide its members with valuable experience in the skills needed for audio reporting, including story research, script writing, vocal performance and recording, package editing, live broadcast production, streaming management, and more.

name: WNUR Sports
description: WNUR Sports is the flagship radio station for the Northwestern women’s basketball team. We also broadcast every football game and home men’s basketball game. WNUR Sports is the only place you can hear the Northwestern Wildcats compete in women’s lacrosse, men’s soccer, women’s soccer, baseball, softball and volleyball. Through live game broadcasts, weekly sports talk programming, and original digital content, we connect Wildcats fans to their teams with timely, in-depth storytelling across radio, web, and social platforms. We provide students with hands-on experience in play-by-play broadcasti

name: WNUR Student Radio
description: Through its programming, WNUR strives to provide a forum for underrepresented music and ideas. WNUR promotes musicians, musical genres, news, public affairs issues, and athletic events often overlooked by major media outlets.We aim to provide an inclusive space for people to learn and express themselves by exploring and promoting underrepresented content, and in turn sharing that knowledge with others.

name: Women in Business
description: Women In Business (WiB) is an open-entry organization established to provide business-minded female-identifying individuals with the background and network to support them in their professional endeavors. WIB's goal is to engage these individuals across a wide variety of academic and professional affiliations on campus in order to catalyze the involvement of women in the Northwestern community, in the business world, and beyond.

name: Women in Computing
description: We want to create a supportive and educational community of any and all women identifying students, researchers, and faculty at Northwestern who are interested in computer science and its applications. No need to be an EE/CE/CS major or minor to join us!

name: Women in Music
description: According to the official website, Women in Music is “an organization with a mission to advance the awareness, equity, diversity, heritage, opportunities, and cultural aspects of women in the musical arts through education, support, empowerment, and recognition.”
